transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? How can I assist you?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in today because I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. I'm a credit counselor, and lately, I'll just sit and stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I end up rereading the same line over and over again. Then I just put off making my calls... it just seems like even simple decisions feel a lot harder than they should right now.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these difficulties been going on for at least a couple of weeks?
Well, it's definitely been longer than a couple of weeks. Honestly, this has been going on since my close friend died... that was a little over two years ago.
Since your friend passed away, have you experienced periods where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Yes, I'd say so. Most days, there's just this... dull heaviness sitting with me. It's almost every day. Even when I try to do things I usually enjoy, like going to the community center or working in my garden... places that used to lift my spirits... I just feel like I'm going through the motions. I'll put a smile on, but underneath, I just feel down.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally taxing?

Yes, definitely. Honestly, I wake up tired even after getting a full night's sleep. And then, by the time I've just done a couple of client calls or gone out to water the tomatoes, my body just feels... well, it feels like I've put in a whole day's work already. It's just this constant lack of energy.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, such as working in your garden or going to the community center?

Well, I still go to the community center and I still work in the garden... I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest. I just... like I said, I feel down while I'm doing them. I guess the joy just isn't really there right now, but I still try to keep up with those things.
Can you describe how your mood has changed since your friend passed away—has it felt like a constant sadness, or more like episodes of feeling very down that come and go?

I don't really think it comes and goes in episodes. It's more... well, it's just constant. Ever since she passed, that heaviness I mentioned has just been sitting there. I don't really have days where I feel completely back to normal and then suddenly feel down again. It's just a steady sadness that doesn't really leave me.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight since your friend passed away?
No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. My appetite has been about the same, and my weight hasn't fluctuated or anything. I still eat my normal meals.
Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living or had thoughts about harming yourself since your friend passed away?

No, no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, it's a heavy sadness, but I've never wanted to hurt myself or felt like life isn't worth living. I just... I just wish I didn't feel so down all the time. But no, I haven't had any thoughts of harming myself.
Have you ever felt like you're not living up to your expectations or felt excessive guilt about things you did or didn't do since your friend passed away?

No, I haven't really felt that way. I mean... I don't feel guilty about anything regarding her passing. We were very close, and I know I was a good friend to her. And as far as my own expectations go, I don't feel like a failure or anything like that. I'm still doing my job and getting through my days. It's really just that constant sadness I mentioned, not guilt.

Have you ever had periods where your mood was extremely elevated, irritable, or you felt like you had much more energy than usual, to the point where it was noticeable to others or affected your behavior?
No, I haven't ever had anything like that. My mood doesn't really go up like that, and I don't get bursts of energy or anything out of the ordinary. It's really just been the sadness.
When you participate in activities like working in your garden or going to the community center, do you find that you no longer feel any pleasure or enjoyment from them, even a little bit?

No, I wouldn't say I don't feel *any* pleasure from them. I mean... I still like being out in the garden. It's nice. And going to the community center is fine, too. It's just... maybe it doesn't feel quite as bright as it used to, because of the sadness. But I still enjoy those things. I definitely still get some pleasure out of them.
Have you found it difficult to concentrate on tasks, even simple ones, since your friend passed away?

Yes, I have. Actually, that's a big part of why I decided to come in. I just can't seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. At work, I'll stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list and find myself rereading the same line over and over. Then I end up putting off making my calls, just because... well, even simple decisions feel a lot harder than they should right now.
Would you say that you've lost most or all of the pleasure you used to feel in your activities, like working in your garden or going to the community center?

No, I think we just talked about that. I haven't lost all the pleasure in those things. I still enjoy my garden and the community center, it's just maybe not as strong as it used to be. But I definitely still like doing them.
Would you say that most activities you engage in, like your work, your garden, or socializing, no longer feel pleasurable or rewarding to you?

I feel like you're asking me the same question again. No, they still feel rewarding. Like I just mentioned, I still get enjoyment out of my garden and seeing people at the center. Work is frustrating right now because I can't focus, but I definitely haven't lost the pleasure in my hobbies or socializing. I still like doing them.
Would you say that you've experienced a loss of pleasure or interest in almost all activities, not just your usual ones, since your friend passed away?

I'm sorry, but we really are just going in circles now. No, I haven't lost interest in almost all activities. Like I just said, I still enjoy things. I don't know how else to explain it... I still find pleasure in what I do, whether it's my usual routine or something else. It's really just the focus and making decisions at work that are the problem for me right now, not a lack of interest.
Would you say that most of the things you used to enjoy, not just your regular activities, have become less pleasurable or less rewarding for you since your friend passed away?

Doctor, I really don't know how many different ways I can answer this. No. Things have not become less pleasurable or less rewarding. I still enjoy my life and my activities just as much as I did before. I feel like you're waiting for me to change my answer, but it's still no. I haven't lost my ability to enjoy things.
Would you say that activities you used to look forward to, like your hobbies or spending time with friends, feel noticeably less enjoyable than they did before your friend passed away?

Doctor, I'm really getting frustrated here. I feel like you are asking me the exact same thing for the fourth time. No, they do not feel noticeably less enjoyable. I still look forward to my hobbies. I still look forward to seeing my friends. Nothing has changed with how much I enjoy those things. I just... I don't know why we keep coming back to this when I've told you it's not an issue for me.
Would you say that your sadness since your friend passed away has been so severe that it has caused significant impairment in your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Yes, I suppose it has. I mean, at the credit office, I've started putting off client follow-ups because I just can't seem to focus or make the decisions I need to. And outside of work... well, I've stepped back from the gallery events and the walking-club outings that I usually make a point of going to. So, yes, it's definitely affecting my daily life.
